definition: An unpredictable error that makes repeated readings scatter above and below the true value; repeating and averaging reduces its effect, and it lowers precision.
An error that shifts every reading the same way, such as an unzeroed balance or heat loss; repeating does not reduce it, and it lowers accuracy.
How close repeated measurements of the same quantity are to each other.
How close a measurement, or the mean of several, is to the true or accepted value.
The range either side of a value within which the true value lies, written with $\pm$ and the same unit as the value, as in $12.35 \pm \pu{0.05 cm3}$.
The absolute uncertainty divided by the measured value; it has no unit and is also called the relative uncertainty.
The fractional uncertainty multiplied by 100, which lets you compare the uncertainties of different measurements.
The difference between an experimental value and the accepted value, divided by the accepted value and multiplied by 100.
The change in a value divided by its initial value and multiplied by 100; positive for an increase and negative for a decrease.
The difference between two values divided by their mean and multiplied by 100, used when neither value is a reference.
The digits of a value that carry meaning: all non-zero digits, zeros between them, and zeros at the end of a number that has a decimal point, but not leading zeros.
Working out the uncertainty of a calculated result from its raw data: add absolute uncertainties when adding or subtracting, and add percentage uncertainties when multiplying or dividing.
Values calculated from raw measurements, such as a titre, a concentration or an enthalpy change; they carry the uncertainties of the readings they came from.
